**Sundhedsvæsenets Kvalitetsinstitut** (The Danish Healthcare Quality Institute) is the national authority responsible for preparing, monitoring, and reporting quality indicators for atrial fibrillation in Denmark [^src14]. It plays a central role in the implementation of quality goals in clinical practice by producing the national quality report [[atrieflimren-i-danmark|Atrieflimren i Danmark]] [^src14]. The institute is responsible for the publication of the [[afdk-2025]] report (and previously the [[afdk-aarsrapport-2023|Årsrapport 2023]]), which covers the measurement period from July 1, 2024, to June 30, 2025, and was officially published on December 12, 2025 [^src10].

The institute defines and publishes various clinical quality indicators and their corresponding [[udviklingsmaal|Udviklingsmål]] (development goals) [^src3]. For example, it is the defining body for [[indikator-8|Indikator 8]], which measures the implementation of structured patient education [^src5], and it publishes [[indikator-7|Indikator 7]], which tracks the incidence of severe bleeding among prevalent patients [^src4]. The reports produced by the institute serve as political and professional steering tools, supporting regional and local improvement initiatives in cardiovascular quality development across the Danish healthcare system [^src9].

To execute its mandate, the institute employs various clinical epidemiologists, statisticians, and data managers. Key staff members contributing to these reports include [[inge-oster|Inge Øster]], [[anders-moller-schlunsen|Anders Møller Schlünsen]], [[miriam-grijota-chousa|Miriam Grijota Chousa]], and [[chresten-gamborg-puggaard|Chresten Gamborg Puggaard]] [^src7]. To ensure data privacy and adhere to strict governance standards, results with only 1 or 2 patient pathways in the numerator or denominator are replaced with a "#" in the published tables [^src10].
